front: In current Modbus terminology, what are the requesting and responding devices called, and what were they called before?
back: The device that starts a transaction is the client (old name: master); the device that answers is the server (old name: slave).
excerpt: In former terminology, the client was named master and the server named slave.

front: On which TCP port does a Modbus TCP server listen by default?
back: Port 502.
excerpt: Modbus TCP or Modbus TCP/IP is a Modbus variant used for communications over TCP/IP networks, connecting over port 502.

front: How does Modbus RTU encode messages on a serial line, and how does it detect transmission errors?
back: It sends compact binary data and appends a CRC checksum to each frame.
excerpt: makes use of a compact, binary representation of the data for protocol communication. The RTU format follows the commands/data with a cyclic redundancy check checksum

front: In the Modbus data model, what size is a coil and what access does a client have to it?
back: A coil is one bit, and it can be both read and written.
excerpt: Coils Single bit Read-Write Input Registers

front: In the Modbus data model, what size is a discrete input and what access does a client have to it?
back: One bit (on/off), read-only.
excerpt: Discrete input R 1 bit (0–1) Read on/off value

front: In the Modbus data model, what size is an input register, what access does a client have, and what does it typically hold?
back: A 16-bit word, read-only, usually a measurement or status value.
excerpt: Input register R 16 bit words (0–65,535) Read measurements and statuses

front: In the Modbus data model, what size is a holding register, what access does a client have, and what does it typically hold?
back: A 16-bit word that is readable and writable, typically used for configuration values.
excerpt: Holding register R/W 16 bit words (0–65,535) Read/Write configuration values

front: Which Modbus function codes read holding registers, write one holding register, and write several?
back: FC 3 reads them, FC 6 writes a single one, FC 16 writes multiple.
excerpt: Read Multiple Holding Registers 3 Write Single Holding Register 6 Write Multiple Holding Registers 16

front: Which Modbus function codes read coils, write one coil, and write several coils?
back: FC 1 reads coils, FC 5 writes a single coil, FC 15 writes multiple coils.
excerpt: Read Coils 1 Write Single Coil 5 Write Multiple Coils 15

front: What does the unit identifier in a Modbus TCP header select when talking to a TCP-to-RTU gateway?
back: It holds the server address of the specific device sitting behind the gateway.
excerpt: In such a case, the unit identifier is the Server Address of the device behind the gateway.

front: What protection does the Modbus protocol itself offer against forged commands or eavesdropping?
back: None: it has no built-in authentication of commands and no confidentiality for the data on the wire.
excerpt: Modbus protocol itself provides no security against unauthorized commands or interception of data.

front: Why do classic industrial protocols generally lack authentication and encryption?
back: They were built for safe, reliable control on networks that were never meant to connect to outside networks.
excerpt: Traditional OT systems were designed to operate industrial processes safely and reliably without connections to external networks.

front: Which organization maintains and supports the PROFINET standard?
back: PROFIBUS & PROFINET International (PI), the same body behind PROFIBUS.
excerpt: The standard is maintained and supported by Profibus & Profinet International

front: What cycle times do PROFINET RT and PROFINET IRT target?
back: RT targets roughly 1-10 ms cycles; IRT (isochronous) goes below 1 ms for drive and motion applications.
excerpt: The RT (Real-Time) protocol for class A & B applications with cycle times in the range of 1 - 10 ms. The IRT (Isochronous Real-Time) protocol for application class C allows cycle times below 1 ms

front: How are PROFINET real-time cyclic frames carried, compared with its acyclic traffic?
back: Real-time cyclic data and alarms go straight in Ethernet frames, with no IP; acyclic data uses UDP/IP.
excerpt: the Profinet Real-Time (RT) telegrams are transmitted directly via Ethernet. UDP/IP is used for the transmission of acyclic data.

front: What application-layer protocol does EtherNet/IP put on top of standard Ethernet?
back: The Common Industrial Protocol (CIP); EtherNet/IP is CIP adapted to standard Ethernet.
excerpt: is an industrial network protocol that adapts the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) to standard Ethernet

front: Which ports does EtherNet/IP use for explicit messaging and for implicit (I/O) messaging?
back: Explicit messages use TCP 44818; implicit I/O messages use UDP 2222.
excerpt: EtherNet/IP makes use of TCP port number 44818 for explicit messaging and UDP port number 2222 for implicit messaging

front: What physical transmission does PROFIBUS DP use, and how many devices can one segment hold?
back: Balanced RS-485 serial signalling, with at most 31 devices connected on a segment.
excerpt: The RS485 balanced transmission used in PROFIBUS DP only allows 31 devices to be connected at once

front: What is OPC UA and which body develops it?
back: A platform-independent IEC 62541 standard for exchanging data from field sensors up to cloud applications, developed by the OPC Foundation.
excerpt: is a cross-platform, open-source, IEC62541 standard for data exchange from sensors to cloud applications developed by the OPC Foundation

front: Which TCP port is registered with IANA for the OPC UA binary connection protocol?
back: TCP 4840 (service name opcua-tcp).
excerpt: opcua-tcp 4840 tcp OPC UA Connection Protocol

front: What message security modes can an OPC UA session use?
back: None (no protection), Sign (integrity only, readable), and SignAndEncrypt (integrity plus confidentiality).
excerpt: NONE 1 No security is applied. SIGN 2 All messages are signed but not encrypted. SIGNANDENCRYPT 3 All messages are signed and encrypted.

front: Which TCP port does a client connect to for Siemens S7comm, and which layer is negotiated next?
back: TCP 102, then an ISO transport (COTP) connection carried via ISO-on-TCP, before the S7 session itself.
excerpt: Connect to PLC on TCP port 102 Connect on ISO layer (COTP Connect Request)

front: What is a fieldbus?
back: An industrial network for real-time distributed control that connects the instruments of a plant.
excerpt: A fieldbus is an industrial network system for real-time distributed control. It is a way to connect instruments in a manufacturing plant.

front: What makes Ethernet "industrial Ethernet" rather than ordinary office Ethernet?
back: It runs protocols that add deterministic, real-time behaviour for control, on top of Ethernet in a factory setting.
excerpt: is the use of Ethernet in an industrial environment with protocols that provide determinism and real-time control.

front: In which sector is DNP3 mainly used?
back: Utilities, chiefly electric power and water companies; it is rarely used in other industries.
excerpt: Its main use is in utilities such as electric and water companies. Usage in other industries is not common.
